data.title: mTORC2 Promotes Tumorigenesis via Lipid Synthesis
data.authors: Guri Y; Hall MN et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTORC2 promotes tumorigenesis through control of de novo lipid synthesis.
data.abstract_excerpt: Dysregulated mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) promotes cancer, but underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. We describe an mTOR-driven mouse model that displays hepatosteatosis progressing to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Longitudinal proteomic, lipidomics, and metabolomic analyses revealed that hepatic mTORC2 promotes de novo fatty acid and lipid synthesis, leading to steatosis and tumor development. In particular, mTORC2 stimulated sphingolipid (glucosylceramide) and glycerophospholipid (cardiolipin) synthesis.

extracted_findings.effect: Hepatic mTORC2 promotes de novo fatty-acid/lipid synthesis (sphingolipids, glycerophospholipids) driving steatosis → hepatocellular carcinoma
